title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and spent about six months in jail after Fargo, North Dakota police accused her of bank theft. She was held nearly four months in a Tennessee county jail awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota. The charges were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records showing she was in Tennessee at the time of the fraud, and she was released on Christmas Eve. Lipps says she lost her home, car, and personal property, and was denied medications and dentures while in custody.

Lipps has filed a federal lawsuit seeking $10 million in damages from the city of Fargo and police detective Lucas Heck. The suit claims investigators relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and surveillance video, and that Heck requested an arrest warrant without further investigation or probable cause. It also says Fargo police lacked policies and training for facial recognition use. The city declined to comment on pending litigation.
